summary: Backend security hardening tested: login rate limiting (8 fails/15min/IP -> 429 with Retry-After), JWT invalidation via iat < password_changed_at, and fresh token returned by change-password. All 8 new security tests pass and all 63 prior regression tests pass (total 71/71).
critical_code_review_comments: server.py is 1150 lines - consider splitting into modules (auth, admin, public) per file-size guideline (>700 lines).
_login_attempts is in-memory only; not safe for multi-worker/multi-instance deployments. Comment in code already notes this; for production, swap to Redis-backed limiter.

_client_ip() trusts the first X-Forwarded-For value unconditionally - in production behind an untrusted proxy chain this can be spoofed to bypass per-IP rate limit. Acceptable if the only ingress is a trusted proxy.
Rate-limit applies only to failed attempts; this is by design and correct (success resets counter). Verified.

iat-based invalidation correctly rejects tokens whose iat < password_changed_at; the +0 skew works because change-password sets password_changed_at first then issues new token (so new_token.iat >= password_changed_at). Verified via test.

Regression: previous test file test_reviews_faqs_password.py used module-scoped admin_token which became stale after the new password-change-invalidates-tokens behaviour. Fixed by switching the fixture to function scope (test-only fix; no production code change).

rca of the issue: Initial test run revealed two test-side issues that emerged because of the new security feature: (1) test_auth_security.py initially referenced /api/admin/audit-log but the real endpoint is /api/admin/audit -> fixed selector + added try/finally to guarantee password restoration even on assertion failure. (2) Existing test_reviews_faqs_password.py used a module-scoped admin_token, which is correctly invalidated by the new iat<password_changed_at check after TestChangePassword.test_happy_path_change_and_restore runs -> changed fixture scope to function so each test acquires a fresh token. Production code under review (server.py rate-limit + iat invalidation) is correct and passing all assertions.
